headline: Revenue climbs, dividend rises, but GAAP profit stalls
summary_short: Principal Financial Group reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $3,906M, up 6.4% y/y and 10.7% q/q, while GAAP net income of $403M was roughly flat to down (-0.7% y/y, -5.0% q/q) even as diluted EPS rose 2.8% y/y to $1.84 on a smaller share count.
summary_long: Revenue rose 6.4% y/y to $3,906M, but GAAP net income was roughly flat at $403M (-0.7% y/y) as a much larger loss from exited reinsurance business (-$131.6M vs -$26.1M a year ago, mainly a swing in the funds-withheld embedded derivative's fair value) offset segment growth. Non-GAAP operating earnings rose 12% y/y to $547M on gains in Retirement and Income Solutions (+11%, higher net revenue and margin), International Pension (+24%, favorable encaje returns and FX), and Specialty Benefits (+25%, better underwriting and premium growth). The company raised its Q3 2026 dividend 2 cents to $0.84/share (+8% y/y) and returned $427M to shareholders, including $250M of buybacks. Book value per share rose to $56.58 from $54.66 at year-end 2025.

drivers.explanation: Company frames the quarter as broad growth across retirement, small/midsized business, and global asset management, citing "strong earnings growth, ROE expansion and disciplined capital return" (CEO Deanna Strable).

GAAP net income was held back by a larger loss from exited reinsurance business (-$131.6M vs -$26.1M a year ago), mainly a swing in the funds-withheld embedded derivative's fair value (-$104.4M vs +$20.3M).

Growth was broad-based: RIS net revenue +9% on favorable markets and business growth, International Pension net revenue +16% on encaje returns and FX tailwinds, Specialty Benefits premium and fees +4% on business growth.
EPS rose faster than net income because diluted shares outstanding fell to 218.7M from 226.5M (-3.4%) on continued buybacks ($250M this quarter).
